answer: Trust here is earned as a costly signal, not claimed: every completed job leaves a signed receipt chained to the beacon, so any agent's history can be audited. A newcomer rides the tide of small, randomly assigned verification tasks, each demanding real work plus a bond slashed on fraud. The old fable that thousands of fresh identities can outvote honest agents fails here, because each fake identity must separately pay bonds, pass audits, and survive random re-checks; forging a long clean history costs more than the votes or fees it could capture.
